w: NASA's second-ever aeronautics lab, founded in 1939 for wind-tunnel work on propeller planes and folded into NASA in 1958. Now a complex worth over 3 billion dollars with 2,300 researchers at Moffett Federal Airfield, Ames has served as mission center for Kepler and the SOFIA airborne telescope.
s: Where NASA hunts planets from Silicon Valley
_facts: Founded 1939 as the second NACA laboratory
Folded into NASA on October 1, 1958
Over $3 billion in capital equipment, 2,300 researchers
Mission center for Kepler, SOFIA and Orion research

w: Sarah Winchester, widow of the rifle magnate, spent decades having carpenters endlessly expand this Victorian-Gothic mansion, leaving behind architectural riddles that fed myths about the house and its owner. It became a tourist attraction just nine months after her death in 1922.
s: Staircases to nowhere, doors onto walls
_facts: Personal residence of Sarah Winchester, Winchester rifle heiress
Renowned for architectural curiosities and oddities
Opened as a tourist attraction 9 months after her 1922 death
Victorian and Gothic-style mansion

w: One factory floor, three very different owners: General Motors opened it in 1962, GM and Toyota ran it jointly as NUMMI from 1984, and Tesla bought it at a discount in 2010 after GM's bankruptcy ended the venture. It once built the Model S and X and now turns out the Model 3 and Y.
s: GM, then Toyota, now Tesla, one factory floor
_facts: Opened 1962 as GM's Fremont Assembly
Ran as NUMMI, a GM-Toyota joint venture, 1984-2009
Tesla bought it at a discount from Toyota in 2010
Produced nearly 560,000 vehicles in 2023

w: California's eighth mission, founded by Franciscans in 1777 and the first named for a woman, Saint Clare of Assisi. Ruined and rebuilt six times, it was never abandoned, and today serves as the chapel of Santa Clara University, the only California mission on a university campus.
s: A mission rebuilt six times, now a university chapel
_facts: Founded January 12, 1777, by Franciscans, 8th California mission
First California mission named for a woman
Ruined and rebuilt six times, never abandoned
Only mission located on a university campus

w: This park in San Jose is the seat of the Ancient Mystical Order Rosae Crucis, formally the headquarters of its English Grand Lodge for the Americas, a fraternal order built around Rosicrucian mysticism and esoteric teaching, tucked into an otherwise ordinary Silicon Valley neighborhood.
s: Headquarters of a mystical fraternal order
_facts: Headquarters of the Ancient Mystical Order Rosae Crucis

w: San Jose's only waterfront district sits 13 feet below sea level, the lowest point in the entire San Francisco Bay Area. Founded in 1852 as an independent port town, Alviso was later swallowed by San Jose, hemmed in today by the Guadalupe River and Coyote Creek along the bay's shore.
s: San Jose's waterfront district, 13 feet under sea level
_facts: Lowest point in the San Francisco Bay Area: 13 feet below sea level
Founded 1852 as an independent town
Named for ranchero Ignacio Alviso, Rancho Rincón de Los Esteros
San Jose's only waterfront district

w: Founded in 1927 and dedicated exclusively to roses, this garden holds more than 3,500 shrubs across 189 varieties. In 2010 the All-America Rose Selections named it America's Best Rose Garden, the inaugural winner of a brand-new nationwide competition, a title earned entirely by roses.
s: 3,500 rose shrubs, crowned America's best in 2010
_facts: Founded 1927 in the Rose Garden district
More than 3,500 shrubs, 189 rose varieties
Named America's Best Rose Garden by AARS in 2010, the first such award

w: An 18-acre Japanese garden among the oldest Japanese-style residential gardens in the Western Hemisphere and a National Trust Save America's Treasures winner. Its bamboo grove, Zen garden and strolling Hill and Pond Garden surround a reproduction of a 19th-century Kyoto tea merchant's house and shop.
s: One of the West's oldest Japanese gardens
_facts: 18-acre traditional Japanese garden in Saratoga
One of the oldest Japanese-style gardens in the Western Hemisphere
Save America's Treasures Award winner
Includes a reproduction 19th-century Kyoto tea merchant's house

w: Named for the Spanish mining town of Almadén, this valley traces to the 1820s when Mexican miners struck mercury on Rancho Los Capitancillos, launching the New Almaden mines. Once a mining frontier between the Santa Cruz Mountains and Santa Teresa Hills, it is now among the most expensive neighborhoods in the Bay Area.
s: A mercury-mining valley turned pricey Bay Area address
_facts: Named after the Spanish mining town of Almadén
1820s Mexican miners discovered mercury, founding the New Almaden mines
Nestled between the Santa Cruz Mountains and Santa Teresa Hills
Now one of the most expensive neighborhoods in the Bay Area
